title: Finite relations of flat module sheaves are locally trivial
statement: Let C be a category in arbitrary independent object and morphism universes and J a Grothendieck topology. Let R be a sheaf of commutative rings in universe r, and assume composition with its forgetful functor to rings preserves sheaves. Assume weak sheafification of abelian presheaves in universe max(r,m), and that its inverted maps are exactly locally bijective maps. Let M be an R-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] in universe max(r,m), flat in the sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] for the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For each U, natural number n, coefficients a_i in R(U) and sections s_i in M(U) satisfying sum_i a_i s_i=0, there is a J-covering sieve S of U such that along every f:V→U in S there are a finite l, coefficients b_iq in R(V), and sections t_q in M(V), with s_i|V=sum_q b_iq t_q and sum_i (a_i|V)b_iq=0 for every q.

source.place: Tag 08FC, forward implication; Algebra Tag 04VX, finite tensor vanishing

proof.text: Let T(V) be the small set of all n-tuples of coefficients over V, lifted to universe max(r,m). Construct Q(V) as the free R(V)-module on T(V), with restriction induced by restriction of labels and coefficients. Let P be the submodule presheaf spanned by the labelled generators a_i e_a. This construction uses no hom-sets as indices and therefore imposes no size bound on the site.

For any presheaf monomorphism P→Q, its sheafification is mono by left exactness of the existing abelian sheafification. Flatness makes tensoring the sheafification mono. The natural comparison between sheafified presheaf tensor and tensor of associated sheaves is an isomorphism, so the original presheaf tensor map is locally injective.

For the given relation form x=sum_i (a_i e_a) tensor s_i in P(U) tensor M(U). Its image in Q(U) tensor M(U) equals e_a tensor sum_i a_i s_i=0. Local injectivity gives a covering sieve on which x restricts to zero.

Use the finite tensor-vanishing criterion with coefficient identities: write s_i=sum_j c_ij y_j, auxiliary relations sum_j e_kj y_j=0, and identities sum_i c_ij g_i+sum_k e_kj z_k=0 in P(V). Projection to the a-label writes z_k(a)=sum_i d_ki a_i because P is generated by labelled coefficients. Set b_ij=c_ij+sum_k d_ki e_kj. The auxiliary zero relations preserve the factorization of s_i, and the projected identities give sum_i a_i b_ij=0. All witnesses are finite, including when n=0.

from.place: Local equational criterion and preservation of its finite witness covers

lean.statement:
theorem local_equationalCriterion_of_isFlatOnSite
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max r m}] [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max r m}]
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r})
    (M : ringedSiteModules.{max r m}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R))
    (hM : IsFlatOnSite M) :
      ∀ (U : C) (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → R.obj.obj (op U))
        (s : Fin n → M.val.obj (op U)),
        (∑ p : Fin n, a p • s p) = 0 →
        ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧
          ∀ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
            ∃ (l : ℕ) (b : Fin n → Fin l → R.obj.obj (op V))
              (t : Fin l → M.val.obj (op V)),
              (∀ p : Fin n, M.val.map f.op (s p) = ∑ q : Fin l, b p q • t q) ∧
              (∀ q : Fin l, (∑ p : Fin n, R.obj.map f.op (a p) * b p q) = 0)
